sonnet.problem: The card says Christ preached "In that Spirit." The BSB only says "in whom He also went and preached." The card picks one reading of a debated phrase and takes a side.
sonnet.rule: A debated teaching is told exactly as written, with no side taken. / Leave open what the text leaves open. Who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

sonnet.problem: The joke doesn't share the core action of the fact. Peter ties Noah's water to baptism as a symbol, but the joke is about measuring water for a recipe. A stranger would say "huh?"
sonnet.rule: The everyday comparison must have the same action. / If a stranger would say "huh?", rewrite it.

sonnet.problem: The joke repeats the punchline shape of card 4: "Friend, I [past kitchen mishap] ... [CAPS word]." The same self-deprecating "I did a dumb thing in the kitchen" shape comes back in stop 2 cards 9 and 11.
sonnet.rule: Each joke idea, comparison and punchline shape is used once per lesson.
